description: Golden retrieval-quality queries for OpenMem. Relevance is judged by exact memory id against the hermetic corpus built by eval/golden_corpus.py (ids 'golden-*'). Three classes: exact_term (queries sharing surface terms with targets), paraphrase (same intent, partially overlapping wording -- keyword mode must still hit via shared substrings), negative/distractor (zero relevant docs exist; any hit is fallout).

judgment_convention.relevant_ids: exact fixture ids; a result counts as relevant iff its id is in this set
judgment_convention.negative_queries: relevant_ids is intentionally empty; recall/MRR/nDCG are trivially 0.0 and fallout@5 is the meaningful metric
judgment_convention.score_threshold: keyword-fallback results always carry score > 0.0 (>=1 distinct term matched), so any returned row above the default threshold counts as a hit

exact_term.description: Queries using words that literally appear in the target fixtures.

queries.note: Topic-wide judgment: every harness fixture answers 'what is the deepseek harness'. Six relevant ids cap recall@5 at 5/6 -- deliberate exercise of partial recall.
Tight judgment: only the GUI/porting fixture covers web boot payload.

paraphrase.description: Same intent as a target fixture but reworded; keyword mode must still retrieve via shared substrings (e.g. 'port' matching 'Ported'). Some share only one term, which honestly exposes tie-break behavior.

queries.note: Mission's canonical paraphrase: hits via shared term 'port' ('Ported'); known lexical traps 'passport'/'Airport' also match 'port' and are expected fallout.

queries.query: approximate nearest neighbor index training rows

queries.note: Single shared term ('travel'); insertion-order ties may rank it below other single-term matches -- an intentional exposure of keyword-mode weakness.

negative.description: Distractor queries about topics absent from the corpus. Every returned row is fallout. Terms are validated at runtime to be substring-disjoint from all fixture content.
